segments.text: Are you feeling boxed in by row, column, or container-based layouts?
If you've ever wanted overlapping widgets, then Stack is the widget for you.
Stack takes a list of widgets  and renders them from the ground up,
one on top of the other.
It's sized by default to fit all  of its unpositioned children,
which you can override  as expanding to fill the Stack's parent.
all of the Stack's children  will be aligned to the topStart,
for all non-positioned  or partially positioned Stack children.
You can use the Positioned widget
to give a particular child  a particular position within the Stack.
Sometimes, that will push the child widget outside of the Stack's bounds.
You can use the overflow property to control whether it runs out of bounds
